The xtask spec test ran 30 tests, all passing, including every_active_requirement_has_a_mechanism_an_owner_and_a_measure and the_real_spec_passes. I could not run the athena-core spec test (the_real_spec_records_every_field) because of the stale build artifact described in findings. It is covered by the recorded CI `cargo test --locked` pass.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs IntrospectionRecord has optional, serde-default fields for other causes, open hypotheses and contradictions. Grep for the field names also finds them in Answer and answer_schema in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs, and the prompt text tells the model to list them.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. In introspection.rs:205-213 the three Vec<String> fields carry #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]. In introspect.rs, Answer has the three fields with #[serde(default)]. answer_schema lists them as array properties and in `required`. SYSTEM_PROMPT adds: "List each other contributing cause in `other_causes`, each hypothesis ... in `open_hypotheses`, and each input fact that points against the cause in `contradictions`. Use an empty list when there is none, and do not invent entries." The test the_schema_and_prompt_ask_for_the_three_lists asserts all of this.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`. A new test feeds an answer with two extra causes, one open hypothesis and one contradiction. It asserts that the recorded IntrospectionRecord holds all of them and that validate() passes. Without the mechanism the test does not compile or fails.
criteria.evidence: The test several_causes_hypotheses_and_contradictions_are_recorded calls the production apply_answer with the real Redactor. It asserts status Recorded, other_causes == the 2 entries, open_hypotheses and contradictions == 1 entry each, cause unchanged, validate().is_ok() and an AnyRecord round trip. A control answer with empty lists writes no keys. The recorded CI check `cargo test --locked` passed on 724b5893172c. Athena's fails-without run (exit 101, does not compile without the fix) shows the test depends on the mechanism. My own run of `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` failed to compile in this snapshot because the target directory holds a stale base athena-data library: the errors say IntrospectionRecord has no field other_causes, but the source has it. That is an environment artifact, not a defect in the candidate.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`. A new test shows that an answer with an unredactable entry or a word the admission scan rejects in a new list is handled like the existing fields: the introspection is recorded as failed, with a reason.
criteria.evidence: Two tests cover this. new_list_entries_are_reworded_blanks_dropped_and_lists_capped shows that a boundary word in a list entry is reworded to 'the person running Athena', which is how the existing fields are handled. a_list_entry_that_cannot_be_cleaned_fails_the_answer shows that clean_texts returns Err("the answer could not be reworded: ...") when the reword step refuses a list entry. apply_answer (introspect.rs:1552-1554) stores that reason in record.failure and returns before status is set to Recorded (line 1683), so the record stays Failed with a reason. findings.summary: The verifier could not build athena-core in this snapshot. The shared target directory holds a stale base-version athena-data library.
findings.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` failed twice with E0432/E0560: no INTROSPECTION_LIST_CAP and no field other_causes in athena_data::records. The source defines both (introspection.rs:179, 207), and cargo did not recompile athena-data for athena-core's build. This is likely left over from Athena's fails-without-the-fix run, which reverted introspection.rs. My attempt to force a fresh build with `cargo test --config profile.dev.debug=1` was denied by policy, so I stopped there. Criteria 3 and 5 rely on the recorded CI pass. This is an environment issue, not a defect in the candidate.

findings.summary: The failure path for a list entry is tested through clean_texts with a stub reword closure, not end to end through apply_answer. The redaction-failure branch has no test.
findings.evidence: The test asserts only clean_texts' Err string. That apply_answer then leaves status Failed with this reason is visible in the code (lines 1552-1554, 1683) but no test asserts it. The plan names this limit.

findings.summary: List entries are not re-checked for emptiness after redaction and rewording.
findings.evidence: `text.split_off(4)` runs before `text.iter().any(String::is_empty)`, so the empty-field check covers only the four prose fields. An entry that cleaning turned blank would only be caught later by validate(), not as a recorded failure with a reason. This is unlikely in practice, because the blank filter runs on the trimmed input first.

findings.summary: 11 files outside the expected deliverables changed. All are mechanical additions of the three empty fields to IntrospectionRecord struct literals.
findings.evidence: Each change adds only `other_causes/open_hypotheses/contradictions: Vec::new()` (or vec![]). The new non-optional struct fields require these edits, and the files are on the planned-files list.
findings.location: status.rs, proposals.rs, evidence_labels.rs, reading.rs, hestia.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, briefs.rs, athena-cli tests (drain, labeled, proposals, review)

summary: The change gives OLY-R1-03 a real mechanism. Introspection answers and records now hold three optional lists: other_causes, open_hypotheses and contradictions. apply_answer redacts and rewords each entry with the four prose fields, drops blank entries and keeps at most 5 per list. validate() refuses a blank entry or a sixth one. Old records still parse and write back byte-for-byte. docs/spec.toml names the mechanism, keeps owner Athena, and its measure names `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` and ends with `status: not shown`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data` (195 tests pass, including the two new record tests and the old-format round trip) and `cargo test -p xtask --test spec` (30 pass, including the_real_spec_passes). I could not build athena-core myself. In my target directory it links a stale base-version athena-data library, almost certainly left by Athena's fails-without-the-fix run, and my attempt to force a fresh build with `cargo --config` was denied. So my judgement of the athena-core tests (criteria 3 and 5) rests on reading the code and on the recorded CI run, where `cargo test --locked` passed on this exact commit, plus Athena's own fails-without-the-fix runs. Remaining issues are minor: the failure path is tested through clean_texts rather than end to end, and list entries are not re-checked for emptiness after cleaning.
